mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has declined monotonically from -27.9% to -38.1% over four weeks, signaling deepening workplace closures or remote-work adoption. This sustained contraction reduces commute-linked retail visits, driving RETAIL_REC further negative over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the mean of the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses to positive growth in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility rebounded sharply from -15.9% (t-1w) to +11.0% (t-0w), indicating a shift in consumer preference toward outdoor recreation. This behavioral reallocation away from enclosed retail venues will suppress RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks as outdoor substitution persists.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 0% after two weeks of negative values
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points in weeks t+1 and t+2 despite sustained PARKS positivity, or PARKS returns to negative territory within one week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has remained severely depressed (range -32.1% to -35.1%), constraining foot traffic to retail corridors. The persistent transit collapse acts as a structural ceiling on RETAIL_REC recovery; retail cannot rebound substantially until transit mobility recovers by at least 10 percentage points.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -30% for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has been between -32.1% and -35.1% across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 8 percentage points over the next 28 days while TRANSIT remains below -25%, or TRANSIT recovers by more than 15 percentage points in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has contracted from -7.1% to -11.0% (t-1w) before recovering slightly to -6.6% (t-0w), signaling volatile essential-goods demand. When essential-goods mobility destabilizes, consumers reduce discretionary retail visits as a precautionary measure. The volatility in GROCERY_PHARM predicts RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed or decline further over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exhibits week-on-week swings exceeding 3 percentage points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 6 percentage points over the next 28 days, or GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes within a 2-point band for three consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen from 6.0% to 7.7% (t-1w) and settled at 7.0% (t-0w), indicating sustained home-based activity. When residential mobility is elevated and stable, consumers substitute home-delivery and online retail for in-person visits. This substitution will depress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks unless RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 5%.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 6% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has been between 6.0% and 7.7% across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 7 percentage points in weeks t+1 and t+2, or RESIDENTIAL falls below 5% in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility are jointly suppressed (TRANSIT -34.1%, WORKPLACES -38.1% at t-0w), indicating a regime of severe mobility restrictions. The interaction of these two factors creates a compounding effect: without commute traffic, retail corridors lose both foot traffic and the economic activity that funds discretionary spending. RETAIL_REC will decline over the next four weeks only if both proxies remain below -30%.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -30% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -34.1% and WORKPLACES at -38.1% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points over the next 28 days, or either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES recovers above -25% in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has reversed from negative to positive (+11.0% at t-0w) while RETAIL_REC remains deeply negative (-24.7%). This divergence indicates a behavioral substitution: consumers are reallocating discretionary time and spending from enclosed retail to outdoor recreation. If PARKS remains positive and RETAIL_REC remains negative, the substitution effect will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS is positive and RETAIL_REC is negative in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at +11.0% and RETAIL_REC at -24.7% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 8 percentage points in week t+1, or PARKS falls below 0% while RETAIL_REC remains negative.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a non-monotonic pattern (declining from t-3w to t-1w, then recovering from -29.4% to -24.7%), suggesting a policy intervention or restriction easing occurred between t-1w and t-0w. If this easing continues, RETAIL_REC will recover further over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if restrictions tighten again, causing RETAIL_REC to fall below -28%.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC increases week-on-week after three weeks of decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls below -28% in any of the next four weeks, or the week-on-week improvement reverses for two consecutive weeks.
